Given a claim and some evidence, determine the stance of the evidence toward the claim.

Claim

molecular profileERBB2 A775_G776insYVMA
evidence typePREDICTIVE
significanceresistance
therapiesAfatinib
diseaseslung non-small cell carcinoma

Evidence

Efficacy and safety were retrospectively assessed in the subgroup with ERBB2 mutation-positive NSCLC. RESULTS: Twenty-eight heavily pretreated patients in the named patient use program had a documented ERBB2 mutation by local testing. . . . CONCLUSIONS: This analysis of patients treated in clinical practice provides further evidence of the activity of afatinib in ERBB2 mutation-positive NSCLC, and suggests that identification of specific subgroups with certain mutations, such as p.A775_G776ins/YVMA insertion in exon 20, could help optimize outcomes with ErbB2-targeted treatment.


Does the evidence support the claim? Use of the following labels: SUPPORTS, REFUTES, NEI. Give your reasoning
label: NEI. While the evidence suggests that the ERBB2 mutation could be used to optimize afatinib treatment, it is unclear if it means the group with the mutation would benefit or should be excluded.

molecular profileDNMT1 EXPRESSION
evidence typePREDICTIVE
significanceresistance
therapiesCisplatin
diseasesGastric Adenocarcinoma

Evidence

High DNMT1 expression was found in 105/127 (83%) or patients (by qPCR assay). Low DNMT1 expression was associated with improved histopathological and clinical response and OS in patients with gastric cancer (P=0.03/P=0.008, P(log-rank)=0.001, respectively). In one cisplatin resistant cell line, DAC treatment and cisplatin had a synergistic effect.


Does the evidence support the claim? Use of the following labels: SUPPORTS, REFUTES, NEI. Give your reasoning
label: NEI. The evidence states that low DNMT1 expression was associated with improved response, therefore we can infer that higher expression would not be associated with improved response. However the evidence does not say which drug the patients were responding to. Cisplatin is only mentioned later in the context of a cisplatin-resistant cell line.

evidence typePROGNOSTIC
significancepoor outcome
diseasesProstate Cancer

Evidence

243 primary PCa, 37 metastatic PCa, and 20 castration-resistant PCa (CRPC) specimens underwent IHC and microarray analysis. Immunohistochemistry (IHC) showed that FGF13 was detectable in the majority of human PCa samples, and FGF13 IHC scores were higher in high-grade prostatic intraepithelial neoplasia, in primary PCa, and in metastatic PCa than in benign prostatic tissue. There was a significant association between high cytoplasmic FGF13 staining and a risk of biochemical recurrence (BCR) after radical prostatectomy. Multivariate regression analysis indicated that high cytoplasmic FGF13 staining was associated with BCR. Results were recapitulated in cell lines and public databases.

Claim

molecular profileEML4::ALK AND ALK V1180L
evidence typePREDICTIVE
significancesensitivity/response
therapiesBrigatinib
diseasesLung Non-small Cell Carcinoma

Evidence

ALK mutation V1180L was found in an H3122 derivative cell line that had become alectinib resistant after being passaged in increasing levels of alectinib. EML4-ALK V1180L and EML4-ALK wild-type were ectopically expressed in Ba/F3 cells, and brigatinib showed strong activity against both variants. The IC50 for brigatinib against EML4-ALK wild-type was 0.95, which is about 3x higher than the IC50 that was observed for alectinib, but about 6x lower than that for crizotinib. In contrast, the IC50 for brigatinib against the alectinib resistance variant EML4-ALK V1180L was 0.49, indicating increased sensitivity to brigatinib over non mutant EML4-ALK.

A clinical trial of 86 patients evaluated concurrent (n=53) or sequential (n=33) treatment of ipilimumab (anti-CTLA4) and nivolumab (anti-PD1). Claim

molecular profileIDH2 Mutation
evidence typePROGNOSTIC
significancebetter outcome
diseasesBrain Glioma

Evidence

Genomewide analysis of 250 low-grade adult gliomas revealed that patients with a wildtype IDH1/2 had significantly shorter overall survival than those with a mutated IDH gene (HR 7.4; 95%CI: 4.0-13.8). The median survival for patients with low grade gliomas was 1.7 years for patients with wild-type IDH (N=55); 6.3 years for patients with mutated IDH and no 1p/19q co-deletion (N=139); and 8.0 years for patients with IDH mutation and a 1p/19q co-deletion (N=84).


Does the evidence support the claim? Use of the following labels: SUPPORTS, REFUTES, NEI. Give your reasoning
label: SUPPORTS. Patients with wildtype IDH1/2 had shorter overall survival, therefore patients with mutant IDH1/2 mutations had longer overall survival which indicates that IDH1/2 is associated with better prognostic outcome.

evidence typePREDICTIVE
significanceresistance
therapiesTrastuzumab Emtansine
diseasesHer2-receptor Positive Breast Cancer

Evidence

As part of a pre-clinical experiment, the efficacy of ado-trastuzumab emtansine (T-DM1) was compared to that of trastuzumab against various HER2 positive cell lines. Conversely, the cell lines harboring PIK3CA H1047R were resistant to trastuzumab in vitro at all concentrations tested (0-10 ug/mL). Further, treatment with T-DM1 on SCID mice xenografted with KPL-4 (PIK3CA H1047R cells) resulted in inhibition of tumor growth. A single dose of T-DM1 >5mg/kg was sufficient to induce tumor regression >20 days after administration.

evidence typePREDICTIVE
significancesensitivity/response

diseasesGastrointestinal Stromal Tumor

These four patients were part of a larger cohort of 397 patients with incurable (i.e. metastatic or unresectable) CD117-positive Gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GISTs) enrolled in the North American phase III study SWOG S0033/CALGB 150105 who were treated with either 400mg or 800mg of imatinib per day. Claim

molecular profileKRAS Mutation
evidence typePREDICTIVE
significanceresistance
therapiesErlotinib
diseasesLung Non-small Cell Carcinoma

Evidence

In the placebo-controlled Phase III study SATURN, using erlotinib maintenance therapy for patients with advanced NSCLC who were selected for response or stable disease after first line chemotherapy, KRAS mutation was assessed. In the KRAS wildtype group, erlotinib showed a significant benefit for progression free survival (PFS) over placebo (HR, 0.70; 95% CI, 0.57 to 0.87, P<0.001). No statistically significant improvement in PFS was seen with erlotinib in the KRAS mutant group over placebo. Significant difference in PFS between erlotinib treated KRAS WT and MUT patients was not seen. Overall, in the intent to treat population erlotinib significantly improved PFS over placebo (HR, 0.71; 95% CI, 0.62 to 0.82; P<0.001).


Does the evidence support the claim? Use of the following labels: SUPPORTS, REFUTES, NEI. Give your reasoning
